queries: WITH grp AS (SELECT f.orderslink AS orderslink, o.dealedge AS side, AVG(f.feerate - f.rebrate) AS avg_net, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM fees f JOIN orders o ON f.orderslink = o.recordvault WHERE f.feerate > 0.0009 GROUP BY f.orderslink, o.dealedge), side_avg AS (SELECT g.*, AVG(avg_net) OVER (PARTITION BY side) AS side_avg_net FROM grp g) SELECT orderslink, side, avg_net AS avg_net_fee_rate, record_count, avg_net - side_avg_net AS diff_from_side_avg FROM side_avg WHERE avg_net > side_avg_net ORDER BY diff_from_side_avg DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: High-rate means feerate strictly greater than 0.0009 (cutoff is exclusive).
Record count is the number of joined fee records in the group (COUNT(*)), including those whose net rate is null because rebrate is missing.
Groups whose average net rate is null (all rebrates missing) are excluded from the side average and from the output, since AVG ignores nulls and null comparisons are not true.
If several orders share the same recordvault, the join would duplicate fee rows; recordvault is treated as unique per order.

assumptions.assumption: 'High-rate' means feerate strictly greater than 0.0009 (the cutoff itself is excluded).

Record count is the number of joined fee records in the group (COUNT(*)), including records where rebrate is NULL, which are ignored only in the average. A record with NULL feerate or rebrate yields a NULL net rate and is skipped by AVG.
If recordvault is not unique in orders, duplicate matches are kept as-is since the request says to match each fee to its order.
Groups whose average net rate is NULL are excluded from the side average and from the output, since NULL > anything is not true.

alternatives.interpretation: High-rate means feerate at or above 0.0009 (cutoff inclusive).
